Here's a table of the top 10 holdings in the NASDAQ-100 index with their market caps and P/E ratios (as of my last update):

| Rank | Company | Ticker | Market Cap | P/E Ratio | Weight in Index |
|------|---------|---------|------------|-----------|-----------------|
| 1 | Apple | AAPL | ~$3.0T | ~31 | ~12.5% |
| 2 | Microsoft | MSFT | ~$2.8T | ~35 | ~11.5% |
| 3 | Amazon | AMZN | ~$1.5T | ~50 | ~6.5% |
| 4 | NVIDIA | NVDA | ~$1.1T | ~65 | ~5.0% |
| 5 | Alphabet (Class A) | GOOGL | ~$1.7T | ~27 | ~3.8% |
| 6 | Alphabet (Class C) | GOOG | ~$1.7T | ~27 | ~3.7% |
| 7 | Meta Platforms | META | ~$900B | ~35 | ~3.5% |
| 8 | Tesla | TSLA | ~$800B | ~75 | ~3.2% |
| 9 | Broadcom | AVGO | ~$600B | ~28 | ~2.5% |
| 10 | PepsiCo | PEP | ~$240B | ~26 | ~1.2% |

**Important Notes:**
- These values are approximate and change daily with market movements
- P/E ratios can fluctuate significantly, especially for growth companies
- The NASDAQ-100 is rebalanced quarterly, so weights change over time
- Some companies (like Amazon) have historically high P/E ratios due to reinvestment strategies
- Market caps and valuations have been particularly volatile in recent years

For the most current data, I recommend checking financial websites like Yahoo Finance, Bloomberg, or the official NASDAQ website.
